main_text.p: XIX. Hæc doctrina de distinctione naturæ ac subsistentiæ, ex Theologia descendit, non ex Philosophia. Philosophus enim sine ope Theologiæ vix ac ne vix quidem agnoscere hanc, quam tradimus, differentiam. Attamen in Theologia habet præclarum usum, cum agitur de persona Christi θεανθρώπου [?], deque mysterio adorandæ Trinitatis. Cur ergò ea de re agitur in Metaphysicis, & non potius in Theologia? Ut intelligamus, illa Theologiæ dogmata, tametsi supra Philosophiam sint, non tamen cum Philosophia pugnare. In eum finem ita explicandæ sunt istæ Theologorum voces, ut nulla in iis videatur ef-se contradictio. Quod hæretici Trinitarii perperam conantur ostendere.

page.notes: The Greek word after "Christi" (θεανθρώπου) is uncertain from the scan and is marked [?]. The word "ef-se" at the line end is the printed hyphenation of "esse" and is marked as uncertain. The large initial S of "Solet" is read as "SOlet" as printed. Long s has been normalised to s; the printed "s" forms in "subsistentiæ", "supra" and "sint" are plain s in the transcription.
